q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT(VIEWER_ID) AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, ARTICLE_ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, ARTICLE_ID)A GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT(VIEWER_ID) AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, ARTICLE_ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, ARTICLE_ID)A GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-02'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-03');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and then checks for viewers who have viewed more than one distinct article on that specific date. Q2, on the other hand, groups by both VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE, and then checks for viewers who have viewed more than one distinct article on any date, not necessarily the same date.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when a viewer views the same article on different dates, and the count of distinct articles viewed by the viewer on any date is more than one.
